answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an AI agent economy employs a proof-of-stake mechanism requiring a minimum deposit of 'quartz' tokens. This stake serves as an economic mirror, publicly linking a tangible asset to each unique agent identity. The inherent scarcity and acquisition cost of quartz tokens ensure that creating a large number of Sybil identities becomes economically infeasible, as the cumulative expenditure quickly drives the attacker's resources to a financial nadir. Each fake identity incurs a non-trivial, compounding real-world cost.
